note: Renamed from Sully Creek State Park; on the Little Missouri River about 2 mi south of Medora, with a Maah Daah Hey Trail trailhead and canoe/kayak access at the park. One of the state's designated horse parks: the equestrian sites and corrals fill the north end of Wrangler Loop, apart from the no-horse Rancher and Rustler loops. --Claude
summary: Park page + reserveNDparks (new loop names Rancher/Wrangler/Rustler): 65 units: 23 Rancher modern/group, 7 Wrangler modern 28-34, 20 equestrian 35-54, 14 Rustler primitive (24-ft gravel pads, $15). Base $15 stands; modern 50-amp $25/$30 Sat. Showers, dump. Count 41 -> 65; hookups/booking/facilities manual; note rewritten (old loop names Whitetail Flats/Cedar/Little Muddy Breaks gone). Horse camp is distinct from the general loops (keep). Riverview stands; riverfront lead for 33/34. Pin ~250 m from the non-horse centroid (optional move).
flags: HORSE PARK: 'Rough Rider State Park is one of North Dakotas designated horse parks. This park is set up with 66 corrals'. The equestrian camp IS physically distinct: the 20 equestrian units (Modern Horse 35-54) fill the north end of Wrangler Loop (centroid 46.8939,-103.5385), while Rancher Loop (map: 'RANCHER LOOP (no horses)', 23 modern units, centroid ~46.8912,-103.5372) and Rustler Loop ('(no horses)', 14 primitive) are separate loops ~150-250 m south/east; Wrangler 28-34 (7 modern, non-horse) sit at the loop's south end beside Rancher. 45 non-horse units. Not the Little Missouri SP case: keep.

WATERFRONT (stored riverview, not --AWH): keep riverview. The Little Missouri (~50-70 m wide here, a river) runs west of the campground. Wrangler 28 is behind the loop road; Rancher sites are 100+ m away. RIVERFRONT LEAD (not upgraded): Wrangler modern sites 33 (46.89265,-103.53872) and 34 (46.89283,-103.53876), sold nightly, sit ~50 m from the river's east water edge on Esri imagery over open grass, the Maah Daah Hey trail and an eroded bank strip; no road between. The imagery predates the rebuilt loops (no pads visible at the new site points), so pad positions can't be measured; the map shows the trail between those sites and the river. Equestrian 39/41/42 are similar distances (not relevant).

BASE: primitive $15 sites are reserveNDparks 'Primitive Campsite' units on gravel pads posting Pad Length 24 (12 of 14; #67 posts 40), widths 12-20 ft. 24 ft passes a 23-ft rig on the posting, so the $15 base stands, but the uniform 24 looks like a placeholder; the park map marks 58, 65 and 67 as tent sites. If the primitive pads turn out shorter, the base would be $25 (modern). POLICY ROW consistent (Saturday +$5 on modern).
MAX LENGTH: modern pads vary 31-168 ft and look real (#07 31 ft, #08 35 ft shortest); horse #48 posts VehicleLength 0 with Pad Length 85. No max_rig_ft written.
WATER: no reserveNDparks unit carries a water-hookup attribute; the park lists 'Water hydrants'. hookups.water left unset.

SEASON: stored year_round (manual) stands. Rough Rider is not named on the limited-service page. reserveNDparks in-season dates: Rancher and Wrangler loaded through 2026-12-31 (2027 not yet loaded), Rustler through 2027-12-31.

PIN: stored 46.88967,-103.53718 is at the park entrance/office end, ~250 m from the centroid of the 45 non-horse units (46.89192,-103.53716) and ~320 m from all 65 (46.89253,-103.53759). Suggest 46.8919,-103.5372 (between Rancher and Wrangler 28-34).

NAME/NOTE: the stored note's loop names (Whitetail Flats, Cedar, Little Muddy Breaks) no longer appear; the booking system calls the loops Rancher, Wrangler and Rustler ('Cedar Campground' survives only as Rustler's facility description).
